text:
Maya Patel: quick heads-up — ran a fusion+prefetch sweep on H100 (mixed models) across seq=64..4096 and bsz=1..8. seeing a weird p99 regression at seq>=1536 when kv-cache is hot. attaching numbers below.

Santiago Ruiz: can you paste the exact command + kernel flags you used? which fusion mode?

Maya Patel: ran with `--kernel-mode=fusion-v2 --enable-prefetch=1` plus our usual rollout flags. command:
```
./bench_attention --model=gpt-medium --device=h100 --seq_sweep=64,128,256,512,1024,1536,2048,3072,4096 --bsz_sweep=1,2,4,8 --kernel-mode=fusion-v2 --prefetch-threshold=256 
```

perf-bot: perf run 2612345678 completed (H100). summary: median token latency +3%, p95 +6%, p99 +12% at seq>=1536 (fusion-v2 + prefetch). full artifacts: https://perf.redwood.local/runs/2612345678

Oliver Chen: hmm. p99 jump but median small — sounds like KV cache spill / prefetch contention. did you see increased memcpy / cuda-sync in traces?

Maya Patel: added a short nvprof trace, here's the critical slice (simplified):
```
[1536] memcpy_htod: 1.2ms 
fusion_kernel: 3.4ms 
kv_prefetch: 0.9ms 
kvcache_lookup: 0.5ms 
post_process: 0.3ms 
-- total (token): 6.3ms (vs baseline 5.6ms)
```

Li Wang: curious — prefetch threads may be competing with fusion kernel for SMs; on H100 prefetch=1 looks safe at small seq but at long seq the KV prefetch bursts overlap with attention kernels and cause scheduling jitter. can you repro with `--prefetch-threshold=1024` (i.e., only prefetch for seq>1024) and see?

Maya Patel: re-ran with `--prefetch-threshold=1024` — p99 drop back to +4% (better). full run: https://perf.redwood.local/runs/2612345699

Zara Khan: that matches an earlier micro-observation — fusion-v2's launch pattern uses fewer waves but longer kernels; prefetch pushes short memcpy waves in between, which on H100 can evict L2 working set. L40S maybe different.

Santiago Ruiz: can you run A100 + L40S? we need cross-GPU behavior before changing kernel selector.

Maya Patel: did A100 and L40S overnight. quick numbers: A100 p99 +9% at seq>=2048, L40S p99 +1% (negligible). So L40S unaffected, A100 worse but not as bad as H100.

perf-bot: artifacts: H100 run -> /runs/2612345678, A100 run -> /runs/2612345700, L40S run -> /runs/2612345701

Oliver Chen: ok this smells like a scheduler / L2 pressure difference between H100 and L40S. Proposed mitigations: 1) add prefetch-threshold tuned by GPU type in kernel selector, 2) fallback to fusion-v1 for seq>1536 on H100, 3) async prefetch (defer memcpy to host stream). Which is easiest to test?

Li Wang: 1) is very low-risk — kernel selector can expose a small table mapping `gpu_type -> prefetch_threshold`. 2) has higher code churn but quick to flip. 3) needs stream-safety work.

Maya Patel: i'll prototype (1) today and push a canary. local patch: `selector.add_rule(gpu_type='h100', kernel='fusion-v2', prefetch_threshold=1024)` — runs look promising.

Santiago Ruiz: also open to a small heuristic: when kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.8 and avg_seq_len > 1024, disable aggressive prefetch. that's more workload-aware.

Zara Khan: agree — threshold-only is blunt. Hit-rate heuristic should prevent disabling prefetch for workloads that actually benefit.

Maya Patel: created PR #3842 (WIP) with selector table + unit tests. running dedicated canary on `dedicated-us-west` with 5% traffic.

perf-bot: canary launched: run 2612345712, traffic 5%, targets: latency, error-rate, cost. will auto-report in 2h.

Oliver Chen: nice. if canary looks good we should land selector mapping and keep fusion-v2 default but GPU-profiled thresholds. we can follow-up async prefetch later.

Maya Patel: noted. I'll post a short follow-up with the canary summary. thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: reaction: :white_check_mark: canary healthy at 2h interim (p99 delta vs baseline +1%). final report in 24h.
